answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with adaptive computational pricing: every new identity must solve a small proof-of-work puzzle before its first trade, and the puzzle difficulty rises steeply with how many identities share the same harbor of network fingerprints. Like layers of shale pressed into a mesa, the cost compounds — a lone honest agent pays almost nothing, while an attacker minting thousands of clones faces a wall of compute that grows faster than any profit from fake volume.
